decisions.quote: Unlike Bransford et al. (1972), I found no significant model type (same/different) by probe type (old/new) interaction effect on the recognition scores. Unlike Rinck et al. (2001), the main effect of model type for new sentences was not significant, although it was in the expected direction. Unlike Jahn (2004) there was no significant model type by scene type (predator/peaceful) interaction effect on recognition scores. Due to a bug in the experiment script, some sentence groups occurred more often than others. Now I aim to replicate Bransford et al.'s, Rinck et al.'s, and Jahn's results, with a new improved script and with a new set of participants.
decisions.location: introduction (line 12); see also q8 (line 94) and q10.question (line 100)
decisions.reason: The source document (10.17605/osf.io/bu3gm) is a prospective OSF preregistration ('Registration prior to creation of data', q8, line 94; 'Data will be collected online in PsyToolkit', q10.question, line 100) for a planned replication of Bransford et al. (1972), Rinck et al. (2001), and Jahn (2004) using a corrected script and a new sample. The shipped quote refers to a prior flawed 2022 online experiment (and earlier class demonstrations) described as background motivation for the registered study, not the results of the registered study itself. Because no results for the registered replication are reported in this prospective registration, the replication outcome cannot be determined from the source.
